title: Divisors, Linear Systems & Riemann–Roch Laboratory
summary: Choose a curve (P¹ as a sphere or a line plus ∞, a Weierstrass elliptic curve with its torus, a hyperelliptic y² = f(x), a smooth plane curve or an abstract genus-g curve), draw a divisor on it with filled points for zeros and rings for poles, and watch the pipeline run: the rational functions it allows, a symbolic basis of L(D), ℓ(D), the Riemann–Roch balance with the nonspecial regime, and the map φ_D to projective space. Flagships: L(d∞) = ⟨1, x, …, x^d⟩ and the Veronese curves, |2O| as a double cover and |3O| recovering the Weierstrass cubic, the chord group law and E ≅ Pic⁰(E) through the Abel–Jacobi integral, Riemann–Hurwitz and a branch-point playground, plane-curve genus, adjunction and an exact Bézout intersection microscope, and the canonical maps of genus 2, 3 and 4. Also principal divisors, linear equivalence, base points and very ampleness, Weierstrass gaps, valuation vectors, Clifford, the Jacobian, symmetric powers, line-bundle notation, a command palette and a narrated beamdswitch deck. Runs offline.
